Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/INFO-01 Informatica

The work is related to a project in fine-grained complexity and algorithms. In particular, it aims to draw connections between diverse fine-grained complexity hypotheses, and to extend the theory with beyond-worse-case analysis. The selected candidate will be responsible for the following activities: • Conducting independent and collaborative research on topics related to the project's objectives. • Developing new algorithmic techniques and fine-grained reductions between various fundamental computational problems. • Contributing to scientific publications and present findings at international conferences.

The research activity will address artificial intelligence and deep learning applied to visual analysis and pattern recognition, focusing on two main directions. The first is class-agnostic counting, leveraging multimodal AI to develop models capable of counting objects of arbitrary categories, unseen during training, from a few visual exemplars or textual descriptions. This aims to create flexible and generalizable counting systems for open-world scenarios. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Physics-Informed Digital Twins for Breast-Cancer Invasiveness Scoring - 2026_CDR_DMAT_1 (Politecnico MILANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milan
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-04 Fisica matematica

The research programme aims to develop physics-informed digital twins for the quantitative assessment of breast-cancer invasiveness. The activity will integrate mechanistic models of tumour growth and invasion with experimental data obtained from in vitro multicellular systems. Particular attention will be devoted to tumour–microenvironment interactions, including active wetting, tissue remodelling, adhesion, friction, traction and cell migration. The physical matematical models will be used to identify latent biomechanical parameters, such as surface tension, viscosity, active stresses, adhesion and friction properties. item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-27 23:59
Institution: Univ. Bocconi MILANO, Milano
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-03 Analisi matematica, probabilità e statistica matematica

The research is part of the ERC MIND project (GA 101219635) and aims to advance the mathematical theory of turbulence in incompressible fluids. It focuses on partial differential equation (PDE) models, particularly the Euler and Navier–Stokes equations, in the low-regularity regimes typical of turbulent flows. The goal is to provide a rigorous, quantitative description of phenomena observed in experiments and simulations and predicted by phenomenological theories, such as Kolmogorov’s K41 theory and Onsager’s ideal turbulence. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: The ubiquity of logarithmically correlated fields (ROMA "Tor Vergata")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-15 23:59
Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma, Rm
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-04 Fisica matematica

In 2012 Fyodorov, Hiary, and Keating formulated a striking conjecture: the maxima of log-determinants of large random matrices behave like those of logarithmically correlated fields. Surprisingly, they conjectured that also the Riemann zeta function belongs to this log-correlated group. While there has been huge progress in proving this conjecture, most of the current results are for integrable models. The goal of this project is to establish new analytical techniques to show that this connection holds for a large class of random matrix models, and more.
